paragraphs: The site at identakid.com presents CENTEGIX Visitu, which helps schools manage campus access through digital visitor check-in, identification, monitoring and reporting. The people it accounts for include parents, volunteers, contractors, vendors and substitutes. The argument for it is that paper sign-in sheets, handwritten badges and manual ID checks leave gaps in visibility and accountability.

Visitors check in on a school-managed device or through a front office workflow, giving a name, the purpose of the visit and a destination. Staff can scan identification, take photos and record the details a campus needs. Approved visitors can receive printed badges showing who is authorized to be on campus. The staff member being visited can be notified on arrival, cutting down on front office calls. Check-in, check-out and related activity are recorded, leaving a visitor history for review and reporting.

Screening workflows can flag potential concerns, though the site says the specifics should be confirmed during implementation. Visitu sits beside other safety products on the site, including a wearable panic button called CrisisAlert. Another is Safety Blueprint, a digital mapping product for directing responders to critical incidents. Beyond schools, the same campus safety solutions are offered to colleges and universities.

quote.text: Every school needs to know who is in the building, why, and when they leave.
